question: How can sparse-autoencoder features be tracked across language-model checkpoints, and what semantic and geometric phases do those matched features exhibit?

key_findings.claim: SAE-Track warm-starts each checkpoint's sparse autoencoder from the preceding one, preserving feature IDs and reducing the steps required for a continual SAE series.
key_findings.evidence: Sequential residual-stream checkpoints are paired with inherited encoder/decoder weights; normal independently trained SAEs and reverse-order tracking provide controls for path dependence.

key_findings.claim: Manual inspection suggests token-level features appear early while concept-level features gradually form through specialization, transformation, or maintenance patterns.
key_findings.evidence: A sample of 256 tracked features is labeled from top-activating examples; the authors explicitly acknowledge subjectivity and use geometric measures as additional support.

key_findings.claim: Feature formation is modeled as activations and decoder directions converging toward local final-checkpoint regions, while most directions continue a three-phase drift even after semantic labels stabilize.
key_findings.evidence: Progress measures, cosine distributions and vector trajectories across Pythia checkpoints show gradual localization, early rapid alignment, slower drift, and final stabilization; multiple scales/layers reproduce the qualitative pattern.

method.core_idea: Turn isolated SAE snapshots into a longitudinal coordinate system by warm-starting and retaining feature identities across model checkpoints.
method.mechanism: Train SAEs on successive residual streams, inspect top activations, compare current decoder vectors and activation neighborhoods to their final counterparts, and audit robustness through reverse tracking and alternate similarity metrics.
assumptions: Warm-started latent IDs continue to denote the same feature rather than forcing an artificial correspondence.
Top-activating examples support reliable token/concept semantic labels.
Pythia and Stanford GPT-2 checkpoints represent broader LLM feature development.

techniques.role: Maintains an economical sequence of aligned sparse dictionaries.
Measures convergence of activation and decoder neighborhoods toward final features.
Separates semantic stabilization from geometric direction stabilization.

evaluations.setting: Residual-stream checkpoints from Pythia 160M/410M/1.4B and Stanford GPT-2 scales/layers.
evaluations.metric: SAE convergence steps, manually labeled transition types, progress measures and decoder cosine/trajectory plots.
evaluations.result: Warm starts converge faster; concept features form gradually and many directions drift after their semantics appear stable.
evaluations.baseline: Independently initialized SAE snapshots, reverse-order tracking, and alternative similarity measures.

limitations: Models are mid-scale because most frontier models lack dense public checkpoints.
Manual interpretation of 256 features is subjective and not a population estimate with annotation reliability.
Warm starts can manufacture continuity or suppress feature splitting/merging.
SAE reconstruction/sparsity choices affect which features exist and how they match.
failure_modes: A latent can swap meaning while retaining its index.
Feature splitting, merging, birth and death may be misread as smooth drift.
Checkpoint spacing can miss abrupt transitions.
reusable_insights: Longitudinal interpretability requires identity uncertainty, not just a nearest-feature match.
Semantic stability and vector stability are different observables.
Forward/reverse and independently initialized controls are essential for continual dictionary learning.
open_questions: Can optimal transport or birth-death matching quantify feature identity uncertainty?
Do causal feature effects stabilize before or after semantic labels and directions?
Do the phases persist in larger instruction- and RL-trained models?

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Cunningham et al. establish interpretable sparse features at a fixed model state; the target adds checkpoint-to-checkpoint identity and temporal dynamics.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Large-scale SAE training and evaluation baseline.
competitive_landscape.difference: Gao et al. study dictionary size, sparsity, dead latents and feature-quality scaling at fixed activations; the target studies evolution across base-model training but at much smaller scale.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Universal Feature Spaces Across Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Lan et al. match independently trained models through activation correlation to test universality; SAE-Track inherits identities through time within a training run and studies formation/drift.

novelty_assessment: SAE-Track is a useful temporal measurement tool and the separation of semantic from geometric stabilization is a defensible new observation. The feature identities remain method-dependent, so the results should not be presented as a unique decomposition of what the LLM learned.
reviewer_notes: Read all 34 extracted pages, including reverse tracking, alternate metrics, different scales/layers, examples, and limitations. Primary competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23.
